title: Backtracking Pruning
summary: Stop exploring a branch as soon as a hard constraint or valid bound proves that no completion below that partial choice can succeed or improve the answer.
recognition_signals: partial choices can become permanently invalid
future additions cannot repair a violated constraint
a mathematical bound can prove the branch cannot beat the current best
core_rules: Prune only from a proof, not because a branch merely looks unlikely.
A pruning condition must remain valid for every possible completion below the current state.
structural_steps: test hard constraints and valid bounds
return immediately when failure or non-competitiveness is proven

common_confusions.distinction: Choose/explore/undo defines the search lifecycle. Pruning is an additional correctness-preserving rule for deleting branches before exploring them fully.
